messages.text: Senior center had that screen on again this morning. Same four faces talking over each other.
You still saving that map with the blue lakes north of the line?
River trail at 10? You don't have anywhere to punch in, so no excuses.
I stepped out after the weather. Tell me who actually got the sidewalk ramp fixed and I will listen.
It is in the drawer with the passport card. Mary says I can look, not book.
I can make 10. Need to stop by the shed first and put those old cabinet clamps back before Mary notices.
Ha. Fair. River trail at 9:30? We can settle the important business: Mustangs pitching.
Smart woman. Check the tires before you go pointing the car at mountain roads.
Bring that little sanding block you made for my grandson's shelf. He wore it smooth already.
That is better use of breath. I will bring my cap.
First the checkup, then the car, then see what is left in the envelope.
Same kind I used for the diner shelves years back. Mine were always simple tools and a handshake.
Dad, I looked at the clinic portal. The intake page still has the same blank boxes from last year.
Good. I did not want to guess on those old paperwork questions.
Do not guess. For the sections asking for branch dates, discharge paper number, or case number, leave them empty unless you actually have documents.
Then empty is right. I will sign after supper when Mary has the glasses out.
Dad, the clinic portal says they can do the arm stuff on Friday morning if you still want both done together.
That is fine. I would rather hear it from them than from those forwarded things people send around.
Ask for Nurse Carla if she is there. She explains it plainly. I can look at the handout after supper too.
Send me what you see. I will bring the paper Mary keeps in the blue folder.
Doctor at 10:30. Bring the blue folder and the envelope from Dr. Haynes with the March numbers.
Doctor at 10:30. I put the blue folder by your coat and marked the new page with a yellow slip.
I see it. I will bring the folder and the small notebook from the kitchen table.
I have it by the calendar. I also crossed Bear Paw Cafe off for Friday and wrote soup instead.
Good. After that, stop by Ruth's if she still has eggs. Joe called too, but call him back after lunch.
Good. Leave the Boot Barn card on the fridge. We can look again after the gas bill clears.
The old pair will make it another stretch if I keep them by the back door.
All right. I will leave the clinic sheet on the counter when I get back.
I can bring eggs Thursday. You still want that coffee tin of blue size-11s from Auntie's box?
Yes. The girls asked for small hoops, and the blue will sit right with the white center.
Your hands better not be doing all those tiny rows tonight. Mary will give me that look.
Just sorting colors. I still need to sand the little cedar frames and put a second coat on the horse panel.
Can you and Mom do Sunday at 6? Lena said she can get on after she drives back from Great Falls.
That works. You still on the late shift in Billings this week?
Yeah. Work orders piled up after the gym leak, so I may be dusty on video.
We will take dusty. I will tell Mary to put you and Lena both on the kitchen calendar.
Heard Jalen got pulled over coming back from practice. Nothing on the truck, just questions.
That boy keeps his papers cleaner than I ever did. Still, I tell him to keep both hands where they can see.
Yeah. School board meeting Thursday has that road stop item. You want me to call in?
Listen if you can. I want to hear if they are bringing in elders and clinic folks before the next round of calls.
Walk after coffee? Wind looks mean but not terrible.
Short loop. Mary has me sorting that drawer with the 1994 furnace slip and the Spokane crew letter.
Still keeping that letter? You could have chased those west-side checks.
Maybe. Then I would have missed too many suppers, kids' games, and plain mornings on this trail.
River path is clear enough. Short loop after coffee?
Yes. I have the small notebook with me too. Want to look at a rough park-table layout after we walk.
As long as you do not make me draw straight lines. Put the chairs where the old knees can sit.
That is the idea. Shade side for them, open side for the kids with seed cups and paper.
Senior center has cards after the river loop. Earl said he is bringing his brown cooler again.
I will walk, then coffee only. If they crowd by the back door with that haze, I will sit by the window.
Window table it is. I am not babysitting you through Earl's stories anyway.
Good. I want my head clear before Mary has me sorting receipts.
Clinic packet is on the table. For that separate background question, I marked No like last year.
Good. I still need to fill the line for Fort Belknap, not leave it blank.
Bring the blue folder. The copy from Harlem has the number they always ask for.
I can drop eggs after lunch. You two need anything from outside town?
If you have a little sage left, Mary wants it for the pot with beans tonight.
Sage I have. Are those little tomato cups on your porch still alive or did March win?
Still alive. The flour jar was needier this morning than they were.
If you and Mary are coming after supper, I will set two dozen eggs by the back door. Road is muddy past the cottonwoods.
We can come out before dark. I will bring that old photo envelope too.
Good. Calvin asked about those pictures when he rang from Mesa last night. I told him you still had the box.
I will try him Sunday if the time change does not trip me up.
Dad, Marcus got tailed again leaving the gas station after work. Kids heard about it before supper.
Tell them I know that tight feeling. I can talk with them Sunday, not to scare them, just so they do not pretend it is nothing.
Good. I am no good at the long talk. They listen better when you bring up old Havre stories.
I will keep it plain. What happened then and what they see now belong in the same conversation.
You already been down by the cottonwoods? Wind cut right through my jacket.
Went before Mary had the skillet warm. Saw the first yellow flash by the fence line, then just sat a while.
That open stretch wakes a man up. Save your legs for Wednesday, old timer.
I came back slower than I went out. The river was low but it sounded good.
Your envelope is still by the toaster. I put the small forum flyer inside it.
Good. I want to check the county names against what they said about the clinic and the school roof.
Bring your glasses. You always read the back page twice before you seal it.
I know. The top names were easy. The two county boxes need another look.
I put the blue folder by your chair. Do the right-hand page before you start sorting beads.
Already warmed it up. I am only making the little tray sets today.
Good. No big wall piece before lunch. Last January was enough.
I remember. The students can handle the larger part when they come by.
Sit a little longer before we go to the grocery. Carla said fifteen minutes, and I am watching the clock.
I am fine. One arm feels heavier than the other, that is all.
Lena texted that the paper matches what Dr. Harlan told you last fall.
Good. I will keep their paper in the folder so I do not mix it up with talk from the senior center.
Dad, did that envelope from Marla's office have what you needed for the county senior form?
Yes. Mary tucked it behind the 2025 return copy. We only had the deed letter and tax bill for the house.
Good. I wondered if you needed anything from a bank.
No bank packet for that place anymore. Marla said the stack was lighter than most.
I can drive up Saturday morning. Do you and Mom want me to vacuum behind the washer or just handle the porch boxes?
Mary has a short list on the fridge. Porch boxes first, then the blue bin in the spare room if your hands are free.
I will bring the kids' sleeping bags in case we stay over. Please do not make up the back room until I know.
We made a small pot of soup for supper. If you all come, Mary said she can add beans and sourdough.
I wrote the two March deposits in the blue book. 1,720 cleared yesterday and 1,680 shows for Monday.
Good. I will not move anything until the light bill and the clinic charge show.
Please leave that 400 page alone. If the washer part comes in, we will decide after supper.
I know. I can cover it if I have to, but I would rather wait one more day.
You bringing that little notebook to supper again? Aunt Bernie will hide if she sees you coming.
Only asking about the bread oven and the words Grandma used when she was pleased. No trapping anybody.
Ha. Put in the part where you burned the first batch. Kids need to know you were not born wise.
That part stays. Mistakes teach better than clean stories. I will bring beans and not leave Calvin's grumble sitting there.
You still hauling those cedar offcuts to the center Tuesday?
Just the small crate. Mika and Jace are picking through the straight pieces after school.
Bring the light box then. Save your hand. Those two can carry more than they let on.
I will make them do the lifting and pay them in soup if Mary has extra.
I put the kettle on. Leave the clinic papers in one stack and do not keep sorting them.
I am at the table. Notebook is open. I found the Gillian Welch disc in the drawer.
Good. Play it low enough that you can still hear the kettle. I will read in the front room.
That works. I will write three lines and stop.
You left the blue notebook by my chair. Want it by the bed?
Yes, please. My head kept picking at that bill after supper.
Put it on paper and leave the clinic envelope for morning. Tea is on the stove.
I will do one page after tea, then lights low.
I found that picture of us on 9th Avenue. You, me, Calvin, Ma in her lunch shoes, Dad still holding a hammer.
Keep it safe. That was the year the back room had two extra cousins sleeping in it for a while.
I remember. Calvin snored louder than the furnace. Ma still got up before light to tie that white apron.
Dad would already be checking whose steps or door frame needed fixing before breakfast.
You still want me to bring that jar opener next time? Found one with the big rubber handle.
Yes. Mornings my fingers do not care for tight lids. The weekly pill case is filled, though.
Good. Do the small loop before supper if the weather holds. Mary said you were skipping chips again.
Small loop sounds right. Knees were stiff after church steps, so I am not pushing it.
Kids liked the picture of the blue-and-white piece. You see my note under it?
Just saw it when I opened the phone after supper. I missed it this morning.
A woman from Billings asked if you mail those.
I told her I usually hand them over when somebody is coming through. Too much fuss otherwise.
Saw you by the courthouse yesterday. You were quiet as a fence post.
That was the point for me. Let the mothers and the younger ones talk. I just needed to be there and hear it.
Hearing it beats turning the TV down and acting like it is somewhere else.
Exactly. Same pattern shows up here, just with different street names.
Short loop Wednesday? I can bring that socket set you asked about.
Short loop is good. The tiller bolt is loose again, and I do not want to buy another part unless we have to.
I will bring the small box. Keep me two of those red starts if they make it.
I marked two cups for you. Mary says to take a jar from the basement shelf too.
I put your cedar pouch by the blue folder. Do not forget it before we leave.
I saw it. I will take the hand drum too, in case they ask for the old song.
And change before your cousin's service at St. Mark's. We can sit with Auntie Rose and leave after coffee.
Yes. I will stand with them, but I am not signing any visitor card this time.
I found Mom's little blue book in the egg room closet. Your line has 4-14-60, same as I remembered.
Good. The clerk copy has the same numbers, but the ink is pale.
Mary will like having two papers agree for once. I can bring it by with eggs after supper.
Mary asked if I still have those extra twin sheets. You got small people landing there Friday?
Just two this time. They will use the back room and go home Sunday after lunch.
I will bring sheets with the eggs. Hide your good pencils before they find them.
Dad, this school drawer front keeps sitting low on one side. Same old hinge style you used to mess with?
Likely the screw holes are tired. Shim it with a sliver, glue it, then set the hinge after supper.
Figured. I still remember you lining up kitchen doors on sawhorses in the yard.
Those doors taught patience. I am sanding two little bowls now, so I will send you a picture later.
River trail sign at 8:30. West bend looked glazed yesterday.
West lot still good for 8:45? No backing out because of a little gray sky.
I will bring the cleats, but maybe depot loop today.
I was looking at the clouds. I will be there.
Good. Bring that Mustangs schedule too. I want to see which Friday Thomas was talking about.
Fine. I will be there. No heroic business.
If you are standing there, I will at least get past the first bench.
In my coat pocket. If you start fast, I am taking the short bend first.
Short loop today? I want to ask you about that meeting before coffee.
Short loop is fine. They sounded decent when the old woman spoke, quiet when Aaron's nephew told his story.
Figures. Did anybody mention sending someone besides two uniforms when a person is yelling at shadows?
One lady from the clinic did. I wrote her name down for the next council packet.
Trail is clear enough. We can do the bench-to-bridge stretch and call it good.
That works. I took the morning tablet and had oatmeal, no sausage today.
Walk after coffee? Saw those kids at the center wearing your red-and-black pieces yesterday.
Look at you behaving. Bring gloves if your hands are cranky. I am not tying your shoes.
Short loop only. I want to check the edges before they head to the school dinner.
Gloves packed. Knees get the short route today, pride can stay home.
They looked sharp. One boy kept touching his collar like he was afraid it would fly off.
He made most of that row himself. I only fixed the knot and talked him through the middle design.
Did the 6:30 quiet timer help before the blood pressure check?
Some. I sat through the bell and the numbers looked better than Sunday.
Good. Keep the notebook nearby too, especially when the same question keeps circling.
I wrote the question down and shut the book. That made breakfast easier.
Mom said the office gave you two paper options. Please send me a photo before you choose anything.
Mom sent me a photo of the grocery page. Are you both trying to hold this month closer to 2,700?
I will. The larger one waits. We are doing beans and cornbread Saturday instead of town food.
That is the hope. February got away from us with the tires and the extra pharmacy trips.
Then do the beans and soup first, and wait on the big meat pack unless it is marked down.
That is fine. Also, do not wear the cracked soles on the icy steps if Ruth comes by with eggs.
Mary already put a note on the fridge. I will listen.
I put cardboard liners in them for now. I will watch the steps.
Ruth said she can stop here after the elder lunch if your hands are still sore.
Tell her I can lift the small tubs. She should not haul everything.
Calvin left a message while you were outside. He said no hurry, just call when you sit down.
I will call after Ruth leaves. Easier to hear then.
Marla called. She wants the small green folder, not the whole file box.
The one with the bank interest, pension papers, and county house notice?
Yes. She said no extra statements showed up for us again.
I will bring it after lunch. The deed copy is still clipped inside.
I put the oil change estimate beside the blue folder.
Good. I was looking at that cabin outside Banff again, the small one away from the road.
Look is fine. We still need the medicine refill, the fair check, and Lena's visit dates on the big calendar.
I will leave the card in the folder. Same Havre address as always on the forms.
I put the blue photo box by your chair. Rest your hand before you start sorting.
Found Dad's awl and the little Montana fair ribbon. I want the bead edge steps beside that story so it makes sense.
Supper first. Then tea. I will read while you write two pages, not ten.
Two pages. After that I will sharpen Ruth's kitchen knife and call Joe back before the evening gets hard.
Cousin Mel is bringing those little green tin candies tonight. I told him not to pass them around my egg boxes.
Keep them on his side of the table. I am fine with pie and coffee.
You and your plain plate. Mary said one cup, not the whole pot.
Tell Mary I heard her from here.
Community room has two short tables open Saturday. Want one for your tiny bead things?
One short table is plenty. I will bring sample strips and let people try the pattern.
Good, because I am not hauling that big wooden stand for you again, old brother.
Fair. My right hand still complains when I grip that stand too long.
Dad, did you see the Billings school bond mailer? Same roofing mess we had last winter.
I saw it. I mark the ones who talk straight about buildings, buses, and not selling off every open piece near the river.
Makes sense. Some folks here just follow the red or blue sample sheet.
I never liked being handed a whole sheet. I keep the names that have done right by people here.
Dad, somebody sent me a screenshot saying the school roof money got stolen. You heard anything real?
Send me the board minutes or the district notice, not a picture with no name on it.
Found the agenda. Looks like bids moved to April 2, not stolen.
There it is. Dates and bids beat a hot paragraph every time.
River loop Wednesday? I can swing by after coffee if Mary has not already put you on errands.
Wednesday works. Mary put milk, beans, and bread on the list, enough to get us through Friday.
Good. I will not send you home with extra fry bread then. Tell Mary I said she runs a tight ship.
She does. If Lena confirms the weekend, we will shop again and put the folding chairs back out.
I checked the form you sent. The clinic only needs the first page signed, not the whole packet.
Thank you. Your mother and I were looking at it too long.
No problem. I can stop in Havre on the way from Great Falls Saturday, then Thomas can take the Sunday call from Billings.
That sounds right. I will keep the coffee on for you and save the long stories for both of you.
Mom said the assessor card still has the old back-porch sketch on it. Do you want me to scan it Sunday?
Yes. The porch sketch, the lien-release page, and the yellow envelope from the year Thomas started kindergarten.
I can make one PDF. Also, please do not climb up to look at the loose gutter before I get there.
I will leave the gutter alone. Mary already gave me that look.
I put the blue folder on the kitchen table. The senior center packet only needs your signature today.
I saw all those blanks. They always make me feel like I am missing a paper.
You are not. No DD paper, no file number, no old court slip. Just your ID and the regular signature.
All right. I will bring the ID and leave the rest alone.
I can bring eggs before supper. Do you still want those little pots I saved?
Yes, please. Mary says the grandchildren can decorate some when they come through.
Good. I will not wash off the chicken dust unless you pay extra.
Bring them dusty. I will set them by the bead boxes tonight and sort labels after tea.
Rose wants to show you the ribbon dance steps before we head out tomorrow. Calvin mostly wants to show the loose tooth.
Have them tap the camera icon after supper. Mary will keep me from pressing the wrong thing.
We can do 7:15. They are packed for the trip but not staying in Havre until April.
That works. Tell them I want to see the steps slow enough to follow.
Kids asked why your truck always has those little glasses and that old blanket behind the seat.
Tell them a man needs a blanket when he stops on the flats before town is moving.
They said Billings has too much noise for that. I said Grandpa likes room around him.
Room, moving air, and a little quiet. That is enough some mornings.
You already looking at that little blue icon or are you still pretending coffee comes first?
Coffee first. Then I checked the trail group and your weather complaint.
Good. Someone asked about the round pendant under your picture.
I saw. If she comes to the senior center supper, I will bring it along.
You going to the feed after the river walk, or saving your knees for that big drum tonight?
Short walk only. I promised I would sit in for two songs and help take down chairs.
Good. Take your good sticks, not those cracked ones from the truck.
Already wrapped. I am stopping by the river first to leave a pinch for Dad.
I can grab the end table on my way to supper. Mrs. Hall said the wobble is back.
Bring it by. If the old dowel split again I can set a new one before Friday.
And do you want two dozen eggs or one? I heard folks asking if you still have the red bead strips.
One dozen. I have three red strips finished and two more half done.
Supper is at 5:30 at the hall. They want your star quilt sketch for the honoring table.
I can bring it. Mary says the clinic form finally got sorted too.
About time. Same as always: No on that little top box, then the Fort Belknap part underneath.
I will bring the folder in case Lena wants to check it.
I can bring eggs before supper. Does Mary want me to grab stamps while I am in town?
Yes, please. She has the envelopes stacked by the lamp and says we are down to two stamps.
Tell her I will knock loud so you do not pretend you did not hear me. Also Calvin's boy might stop by with that bead question.
Send him over after supper. I can look at it, then we will get the envelopes ready.
The school boiler room door is sticking again. I used Grandpa's old trick with the shims.
He learned plenty with plain tools and a short notebook. Never wasted a board if he could square it again.
Mary said you found Grandma's recipe cards from the lunch line days. Any chance there is a roll recipe in there?
There is one with her neat writing from after she finished at Havre High. I will send a picture.
You still want those old buckets? I can bring a few next time.
Yes. Good for the potato pieces if the ground stays cold.
I will save the clean ones. Mom said you had soup going all afternoon.
Potatoes, carrots, onion, frozen peas. The loaf is cooling if Mary does not guard it.
I drove by Dehler Park after work. They have the new banners up already.
Send a picture if you pass again. Joe will say the old horse logo was better.
I can check June 19 seats when they post them. You two still doing that longer loop on Wednesdays?
If he is waiting at the lot, I usually keep going past the bend.
You make it through that long family call?
Yes. I shut the back door, poured tea, and put The Chieftains on the little player.
That old player still hanging on. Keep it down or Mary will hear every whistle.
Volume is down. I am just marking a page in the notebook before bed.
Please leave the empty egg carton and two clean jars by the back steps before Ruth comes.
Done. I put the jar rings in the blue pail and moved the tomato cages away from the gate.
Good. Also write down how many cans of beans are left before we make the store list.
The clinic form asks for a place to call during the day. I left that line blank until you look at it.
Leave it blank. Home phone and your number are enough.
I found three old yellow invoices under the bead box. One says 'Chand cabinets' and has only our home address.
That was how I wrote them up. Kitchen tables, back rooms, whatever people needed.
I put the blue pencil marks on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. Do not crowd them together.
Saturday can be the small park loop if the alley stays icy.
That is enough. Shoes by the back door, scarf on the chair.
Dad, for that passport thing, do they want the city typed exactly like on the county paper?
Yes. Mary says copy it as Havre, Montana and do not shorten anything.
Makes sense. The school forms get picky with place names too.
I will bring the paper to Lena when she comes through.
River path is clear. You still walking or did those two little pokes turn you delicate?
I walked yesterday. Arm was only sore that first day.
Good. Senior center had three different stories about it Monday. I told them to ask the clinic instead of the coffee pot.
That is what Lena says too. I listen better when the nurse or Dr. Harlan puts it plain.
Are you coming to supper Friday? Auntie Rose said her grandson still will not drive past the depot after dark.
Yes. If he is there, sit him by me. I will tell him about Dad's old route home and why he picked the long way.
You and your history lessons. Bring Mary too. People need to hear it without everyone staring at a screen.
That is the only way I know how to do it. Small table, plain words, nobody looking away.
I can bring eggs Friday. You two still skipping the senior center fish plate?
Yes, Mary has lentils going. We are keeping the drawer quiet until that Haynes paper is settled.
You and that drawer. I saw boots marked down in the north aisle at Big R, but not by much.
Then they can sit there. My old ones got me to the mailbox this morning.
You still coming to supper? Calvin's boy is worked up about that stop by the grain elevator.
We will come. Tell him I am not mad at every badge, but I want his side written down before it gets brushed off.
Good. Bring your notes from that county thing. Mary said you had names.
I have the clinic lady and the elder panel idea. They need to hear both before summer gets busy.
Saw the photo Mary sent. That little shelf came out square.
Nola did the last sanding herself. Jace chose the red and white beads for the edge.
Good. Make them sweep the floor too.
They know the broom spot now. They also know where Mary hides the cookies.
Maya wants to know if she can wear the blue rosettes for the assembly next week or if they are still drying.
Before you send any deposit, please wait for the blood pressure recheck on the 27th.
They are ready. Tell her not to tug the backing. I set them beside the painted box, not in it.
I told your mother no deposit. Just printing the Icefields Parkway page.
Thank you. Also, if the form asks for address history, use Havre and the old Havre place. Do not overthink it.
She also asked if you will tell the mouse-and-lodge one when we visit. She remembers the funny ending.
I can do that after supper. She has to sit and listen first, same as I had to.
That part is short enough. The long part is waiting on the car and the summer money.
Tea is ready. I am reading in the front room.
Coming in a minute. I am finishing the pencil marks for where the shawl dancers could pass without bumping the plant table.
Leave wider space than you think. Children will run through there.
I made it wider. After tea I will shade in the sitting places.
Community supper table may get lively tonight. Calvin's boy has been passing around that courthouse clip again.
I will sit by the coffee pot. If anyone knows when the elder van starts again, send them over.
You are getting boring, brother. Useful, but boring.
Useful is enough. Mary wants eggs if you have six extra.
We may stop by that place with the neon leaf sign before coming over. Do you want anything from the gas station next door?
Just peppermint gum and club soda. Nothing from the leaf place.
Got it. Kids want chips too.
Chips are fine. Keep the truck aired out before you bring them in.
Found that picture you asked for. You and Mom standing by the lilac, before the front steps got replaced.
Send it. That lilac was barely up to the window then.
Also found your old note about not taking the Seattle framing slot. You kept everything.
Some papers are reminders. Some are warnings. Mary says keep only one box, so one box it is.
River trail is dry enough. Mary already warned me not to let you carry the donation box again.
She wrote it on the wall calendar too. I will walk and keep my hands out of trouble.
Good. After the loop, the senior center wants someone to sit with Aaron about his carving mess.
I can do that. Bring your baseball complaints and I will bring the receipt Mary wants dropped at the desk.
I can stop at the Great Falls store before I drive up. Do you need anything besides Mary’s low-salt stock?
Flour, dry beans, and a bag of frozen mixed ones if it is on sale.
Got it. Are the squash seeds from last year still in that coffee can?
Yes, next to the jar I fed before the sun came up.
Lena said she can look at the insurance letter after her morning desk round.
Good. Did Thomas send the picture from Billings?
Yes. He was under a sink again, this time by the cafeteria.
Ruth is coming at 1:00. Please put the Havre High envelope and your dad's grade-eight booklet on the table, not the floor.
Those two keep busy. Put their notes by the phone so I do not mix them up.
I will. Calvin's basketball clipping is in the same box with the porch-step sketch.
Good. I also want the white apron washed before Lena scans it. The old grease spot may not come out.
That apron saw more trays than our kitchen ever did.
School visitor form came up for summer helpers. They asked for any badge papers or county numbers from before.
I do not have anything like that. Same answer I gave the senior center.
Then leave those boxes empty. I just put your regular ID info on the guest list.
Thanks. I can bring my driver's license when we come down.
I reviewed the scanned packet. The clerk entered the No answer on the first screen correctly.
Thank you. Did she keep the Fort Belknap entry from the blue card?
Yes. I also uploaded the Harlem office copy, so you should not have to explain it again at check-in.
School asked if you ever had old drawer slides like the maple ones you used at St. Mark's.
Maybe two sets in the shed. I bought those myself from Northern Tool back when St. Mark's paid by the piece.
No rush. I can stop by Friday after 2 if you are around.
I'll be here. Friday afternoons are just whatever Mary puts on the wall calendar.
Mom said Marla gave you the stamped copies. Did she need any award letters or payment statements after all?
No. She kept the return, our bank slips, and the county house page. That was enough.
Good. Put one copy in the fire box and one in the blue folder for next March.
Mary already did. She also saved the old release letter with the deed.
I sent you the county page link. The hospital reimbursement part is halfway down, under the March meeting packet.
Got it. I am comparing that with the two mailers from last week before I fill the next envelope.
Look at who answered the elder services question too. One of them skipped it completely.
That matters. I already crossed off the loud one who would not answer about the council agreement.
Mary said you and Joe came back muddy. That means you did more than the little loop.
He kept talking about the Mustangs opener and I missed my turn back.
Ha. I will bring eggs Friday. Tell him I still say Billings needs better hot dogs.
I will tell him. He will have an answer ready.
Eggs are on your back step. You coming to supper or did the appointment papers chase you around all day?
Coming. I had to sit with the timer first so I did not carry those papers into the hall.
Bring yourself, not the papers. Mary said you already filled two pages.
Two pages and the pen is closed. I will be there by 6:25.
Saw the photo Lena sent. Those pendant kits look cleaner than the big panels you used to make.
They are easier to hold, and people learn faster when they each get one.
Good. Keep it that way. You could barely turn a screwdriver when I was up after Christmas.
That visit taught me. I talk through the big steps now and save my grip for the small work.
Still walking tomorrow, or are you stuck rubbing finish on those little bowls again?
Walking. I only have one coat left and Mary wants the kitchen table cleared.
Good. Last time at the center you had people lined up and then complained about sore hands.
They took four bowls and a painted board. That does not happen every time.
Dad, Thomas said you talked with the kids Sunday. Thank you. They asked me why people marched in town last month.
I told them about the courthouse afternoon here too. I mostly listened, but it stayed with me.
That helps. They need more than headlines. They need Grandpa explaining what families here have carried.
I can do that. I just want them to keep their eyes open and still keep their hearts soft.
The kids asked if Grandpa has more pages about growing up near Havre. They liked the part with the horse trough.
Tell them I am adding the willow hoop lesson, Grandma's table prayer words, and the time I mouthed off to an elder and had to carry wood all afternoon.
They will remember that one. Please keep the words spelled how Grandma said them, even if the school spelling is different.
I will. We will eat when you come Saturday, and nobody leaves mad from this table if I can help it.
Do you two need eggs before supper tonight? I can bring them and save you a store stop.
Yes, please. Mary is trying to keep the March page from looking like February.
I saw that face on her at the table. I will bring eggs and a jar of chokecherry too.
Thanks. The 3,400 is mostly spoken for, and I do not want to pull from the 400 unless the washer man forces it.
Senior center called me because they lost your supply list again. I told them cedar strips, beads, and patience.
Add two extra clamps and the green felt. Mika is bringing a cousin this time.
Of course she is. Your garage crew keeps multiplying.
As long as they put things back on the pegboard, I will keep the door open.
You forgot your cap here again. I will bring it when I come in Friday, unless you want to drive out.
Keep it there. Gives me a reason to come by next week.
Calvin called me laughing about that. He said you did the same thing with Dad's black hat when we were kids.
He remembers too much for a man who only calls after the desert cools off.
Walked past the old 7th Street place. Funny how small those lots look now.
Small lot, full house. Ma, Dad, Ruth, Calvin, and whoever needed a bed that month.
Your dad patched half that block, if the stories are right.
And Ma could feed a line of kids, then come home and hem pants before the radio cooled off.
Mom said you left before coffee. Please tell me you wore the warmer gloves.
Had them on. The meadowlarks were loud by the ditch, so I stayed longer than planned.
I figured. You sound better on days you take that first slow hour outside.
The wind settled after sunrise. I brought a little of that quiet back to the house.
Mom sent the paper calendar photo. I see two blue checks already.
Joe is watching the river path for me. If it shines, I am taking the school block instead.
Good. Keep it easy and let Joe fuss. That works better than my long lists.
Saturday morning will make the third check if the sidewalks behave.
We can come Saturday after lunch. The kids want to know if they should bring markers or small shovels.
Both, if they have room. I have paper for them and a tray of starts that need names.
I will pack wipes and old shirts. Please do not carry the heavy bin yourself.
Mary already wrote that on the kitchen calendar. We will keep it light and make soup after.
Before I drive up Saturday, do you and Mom need groceries or anything heavy moved?
Maybe just flour and coffee. We still have beans, frozen squash, and two shelves of jars.
Do you want me to bring the pruning saw back from Thomas when I see him?
Yes, if he is done with it. The Belcourts returned our crate with jam, so I can send you home with some.
I looked at the refill slip Mary sent. Did you pick up the 90-day bottle this afternoon?
Picked it up at 2:30. It is in the blue basket, not by the sink this time.
Mom said your voice was tired after the songs last night. Are you resting it today?
Good. Keep using the big pen for the log. And please let Ruth lift the soup pot tomorrow if your fingers are tight.
Resting now. We were late because I stayed to help put the drum away and sweep.
Mom sent me the photo of the insurance page. The number she circled is the one to call Monday.
Thanks. She has it clipped to the fridge calendar now, beside Thomas's visit dates.
Okay. Also, Auntie Rose said thank you for coming Wednesday. She noticed you stayed through the last hymn.
I will. Also doing the grocery list with no canned broth unless Mary finds the plain one.
I will call after work if you both want me on speaker. Do not let the young artists bury the table in beads before then.
For Rose, I will sit anywhere. Tomorrow morning I will go out before coffee and put down a little tobacco for Peter.
They are coming Sunday afternoon, so Monday is clear. We will keep the page where Mary put it.
I put the remote in the drawer. You said ten minutes was enough after the council vote total.
Good. I wrote down the trash pickup change and the water office number.
Lena sent another long thread. I told her you would read the city notice in the morning.
That works. Tea now, not forty strangers typing at each other.
Dropping eggs after supper. Need me to grab anything from town?
No, just bring yourself. Mary and I are moving boxes from the back room before the insurance man comes Tuesday.
Those boxes from when Calvin said you were foolish for passing on that Kalispell crew?
Some of them. Tell Calvin his foolish brother still has the same lilac and the same supper chair.
I put supper pictures up. Don't wait three days to see them this time.
I will look tonight. I looked this morning and then left the phone alone.
Marlene asked about the red earrings in your photo. Want me to tell her to catch you Sunday?
Yes, Sunday is better. I can bring the pair with the egg money.
School sent home spring clinic forms for the kids. You and Mom already did your stuff this month, right?
Yes. Mine is marked on the card in Mary's folder.
I figured. Lena said the Havre clinic gave you the same answer she found.
When Lena, Dr. Harlan, and the tribal health desk all say the same thing, that is enough for me.
I looked over the PDF. The passport site accepts the Montana certified copy as long as the raised seal shows.
Mary held it to the window. The seal is there, just hard to see in the scan.
Good. Keep the original with the page that says Havre and 4/14/1960, then mail only what the instructions ask for.
I wrote 6:45 on the paper calendar for the Sunday screen call. Lena said Maya and Jonah can go first.
Good. Thomas can send Rose and Calvin after them if Billings is not running late.
I will put the tablet on the stand. The house is quiet again, so leave the folding bed down only if April is still happening.
Leave it for now. Easier than digging it out twice.
For Lena's visit I have tea, lemonade, and sparkling water. Do you still want one small glass set out for the toast?
One is enough. Put me near the kitchen door if Calvin's boys use the porch again.
I will. Please do not take any of their wrapped sweets by mistake.
I will stay with your oatmeal cookies.
If you two head up past Calgary, send me the route first. I can look at road work notices.
Nothing set. We are saving slow and keeping July open for family things.
Good. Take the newer insurance card and the registration. Mountain roads are hard on old cars.
I have those with the passport card and the Havre papers. It would be nice to sit by those cold lakes again.
Looks like I can come up from Billings the second weekend in April. Need anything fixed while I am there?
The porch light flickers and the hall closet door sticks. Mary says we can leave them until you get here.
I will bring my drill. Are the grandkids using the den or should I plan on the couch?
Den if they come. Otherwise couch is open after Mary moves the quilt box.
Mary said the papers won tonight. Want eggs tomorrow or should I wait?

events.title: Porch timer + notebook before coffee
events.notes: 12-minute bell. Write the overnight loops in the small brown book before oatmeal.

events.title: Milk River pullout
events.location: River Road bend, east of Havre
events.notes: Thermos, small field glasses, sit before oatmeal. Check the reeds by the slow water.

events.title: Walgreens pickup, then short river loop
events.location: Walgreens on 1st St, Havre; river trail east lot
events.notes: Bring coupon card. Fill pill box after breakfast. Keep loop easy if knees are tight; skip deli ham on the way home.

events.title: Coffee, phone check, reply to bracelet note
events.notes: Look at Ruth's supper photo and the birthday reminders. If Doreen still wants the small bracelet from yesterday's picture, tell her it can wait until Friday.

events.title: Warm soak, right-hand stretches, sort small kits
events.notes: Use clinic sheet from blue folder. Four bead trays for Thursday demo. Leave the large frame in the back room.

events.title: Kitchen table bill folder
events.notes: Meter card, pharmacy receipt, property tax envelope. Set out two mugs before Mary starts sorting. Text Lena a photo if the clinic form still looks wrong.

events.title: Senior center loop
events.notes: Use the paved side by 5th Ave if the shaded curb is slick. Coffee afterward only if hands stay warm.

events.title: Kitchen table receipts with Mary
events.notes: February receipts stack: groceries, gas, copays, power bill. Pencil total came to 3,096. Keep the 400 line in the back page untouched unless the furnace man calls.

events.title: Courthouse drop box before walking group
events.notes: Bring sealed envelope from kitchen counter. Recheck school board names, clinic levy note, elder van line, and Beaver Creek access item.

events.title: North closet boxes
events.notes: Set aside the Havre photo packet with Ruth and Calvin. Keep Ma's white lunch apron, sewing tin, and the envelope with her graduation paper. Move Dad's old plane, brace, and grade-eight arithmetic booklet to the lower shelf.

events.title: Drop folder at Hi-Line Tax & Bookkeeping
events.notes: Bring W-2/R forms, bank interest slip, county house statement, and last year's blue copy.

events.title: Open table: cedar scraps and bead trays
events.notes: Clear the bench by 3:30. Put out clamps, sandpaper, blue bead box, and the old coffee can for donations.

events.title: Notebook hour at kitchen table
events.notes: Sort school-house photo, Dad's awl, and bead edging sample. Check spelling of the old greeting before writing it down. Keep tea on and radio low.

events.title: Tea, notebook, two sides of records
events.notes: Start with the Dylan side Mary set out. Keep little speaker at 2 while bills are on the table.

events.title: South window starts and shelf count
events.notes: Tomato trays by the window. Check squash packets, bean jars, canning lids, twine, hoe handle, and the spare mower belt before lunch.

events.title: River trail with Joe
events.notes: Try north loop if wind stays down. Bring cap from last Billings game so Joe can settle that old pitcher argument.

events.title: County clerk copy request
events.location: Hill County Courthouse, 315 4th St, Havre, MT
events.notes: Bring driver's license, checkbook, and the passport form with the date/place boxes still blank.

events.title: Sort bowls, small figures, bead trays
events.notes: Check price tags from last winter box. Put $120 from February envelope into Mary’s records folder.

events.title: County listening night
events.notes: Ask about ride-alongs with clinic staff, elder introductions before summer events, and how complaints from younger guys are tracked. Thank Deputy M. for helping Mrs. Azure last winter.

events.title: Singers at community hall
events.notes: Bring hand drum, cedar pouch, and the small blanket. Leave early enough to set chairs for the elders.

events.title: Clinic nurse table - COVID card and flu slip
events.location: Northern Montana Family Medical Center, Havre
events.notes: Bring blue folder, Medicare card, and Lena's printed portal note. Ask Nurse Carla about spacing and wait 15 minutes before leaving.

events.title: Check county road notice, then turn set off
events.notes: Look up the plow route update and clinic parking note. No leaving the set running through supper.

events.title: Screen time with Lena's house
events.notes: Have charger plugged in. Ask Maya about spelling test and Jonah about the cardboard bridge.

events.title: Call Haynes office after checking statement
events.notes: Ask whether the crown estimate can sit until April. Move noon at Bear Paw to soup at home. Check Boot Barn flyer before tossing it.

events.title: Trip folder review
events.notes: Compare September rooms near Jasper and Lake Louise. Hold off until clinic note, tire estimate, fair booth fees, and July ceremony dates are known. Keep Havre utility bill copy with ID papers.

events.title: Shop table with youth group
events.notes: Bring tackle box trays, needles, thread, cedar blanks, small paint jars. Finish two pairs for Friday outfits if hands hold up. Leave last 20 minutes for the old winter camp account.

events.title: Community supper with Ruth
events.notes: Bring deviled eggs container back to Ruth. Ask for coffee or water. Sit inside, away from the porch table.

events.title: Call Calvin before supper
events.notes: Try the 602 number. Ask if he wants copies from Ruth's photo envelope.

events.title: Check folding tables + seed trays
events.notes: Measure two long tables. Bring pencil roll, masking tape, extra labels. Ask about chairs for elders and space for children to pot starts.

events.title: Courthouse lawn listening circle
events.notes: Bring folding chair. Stand near back if hands are aching. Mostly listen; no need to speak unless asked.

events.title: Video call: Lena after Great Falls drive, Thomas after Billings shift
events.notes: Ask Lena about the clinic packet. Ask Thomas whether the gym leak is fixed before spring activities.

events.title: Counter jar, soak beans, check porch trays
events.notes: Use 1 cup flour. Pull canned tomatoes from lower shelf. Look at onion sets and carrot packet before breakfast.

events.title: Hill County treasurer window
events.notes: Bring blue folder: tax notice, insurance page, 1996 siding receipt, checkbook.

events.title: Update clinic forms - blue folder
events.notes: Use same answers as 2025 packet: separate first page answer stays No; second page needs Fort Belknap line and copy from Harlem office.

events.title: Senior center volunteer packet
events.notes: Bring photo ID and blue folder. Sign pages 4 and 5. Leave agency ID, branch dates, badge number, docket number, and facility number blank unless clerk says otherwise.

events.title: Sort old cabinet papers with Mary
events.notes: Look for receipt pads, tool bills, Ray's Diner shelves, church kitchen drawers, and the blue folder. Mary says no company packet in that box.

events.title: Sit with Mary: clinic forms and March bills
events.notes: Use blue folder, check due dates, call Lena if the clinic page is unclear.

events.title: Library room: small boxes, sanding, bead edge
events.notes: No fee. Bring sample lid, extra awls, waxed thread, and sign-in sheet from front desk.

events.title: North fence stop
events.location: County road past the grain bins
events.notes: Bring pouch from coat pocket. No phone sounds. Watch the wires and stubble before breakfast.

events.title: Breakfast + pill case check
events.notes: Refill slot should last through Saturday. Write down morning numbers. Toast, eggs, fruit; leave the salt shaker in the cupboard. Ten-minute walk after dishes if hands loosen up.

events.title: After river trail: porch recorder
events.notes: Ask Joe about road crew winters and old ballfield names. Mark which stories are his to approve. Add one paragraph on learning to listen before giving advice.

events.title: Trail, coffee, box score
events.location: River trail east entrance; senior center after
